title: Private delivery safeguard pipeline for immutable upgrades
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Scope: implement a resilient, declarative upgrade delivery pipeline for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that orchestrates component upgrades and schema migrations with strong preflight checks, LTS channel awareness, and automated rollback gates. Goal is to provide an immutable upgrade flow (image + manifest) which: 1) validates customer manifests and operator compatibility, 2) runs non-destructive dry-run migrations, 3) stages changes to canary nodes then full fleet with traffic siphoning and KV cache warmups, and 4) enforces rollback and LTS policies when safety checks fail.

Why: customers running Private expect predictable, low-risk upgrades and auditability. Current ad-hoc workflows lead to time-consuming manual intervention and inconsistent rollouts across on-prem footprints.

Proposed approach: deliver a control-plane driven "upgrade plan" resource (YAML) that declares ordered steps: manifest-validate -> dry-run-migrations -> canary-deploy -> migration-run -> traffic-shift -> monitor & gating -> finalize. Each step exposes explicit success/failure criteria and human-in-the-loop escalation. Use existing runtime image SHA pinning and two LTS channels (lts-stable, lts-fast) to gate version progression.

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- CLI: `rwi private upgrade plan apply --file plan.yaml` creates a plan and returns a human-readable execution log.
- Preflight: manifest validation covers Kubernetes versions, CRD compatibility, and KMS/HSM config checks; fail fast with descriptive errors.
- DB migrations: support dry-run mode that executes migrations against a cloned schema snapshot or runs validation queries; migrations are idempotent and recorded in an audit table; automatic abort on non-idempotent changes unless explicit override provided.
- Canary: plan can target 1-3 nodes for canary; automated health checks for 10m post-deploy before promoting.
- Rollout gates: configurable SLO thresholds (latency, error-rate, db-error-rate) with automatic rollback and annotated reason.
- Observability: plan exposes per-step logs, Prometheus metrics, and a Console page with token-level cost/latency deltas.

Non-goals: building a new config management system or replacing customer IaC. We will integrate with customer manifests and existing k8s tooling (helm/kustomize).
comments: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting — alignment with PM and Security. Action: produce initial plan CRD schema. (owner: Daniel)

2026-02-22: Design review — decided to prefer immutable image+manifest pinning over in-place operator upgrades to simplify rollbacks. Trade-off: slightly larger upgrade artifacts but simpler evacuation logic.

2026-03-01: Architecture review — Security flagged KMS changes as high risk; added extra preflight check to verify KMS key access for migration jobs. See Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Private+Delivery+Safeguard+Pipeline
2026-03-04: PR opened for control-plane plan API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/127 — early feedback from infra: need stronger idempotency guarantees on migration runner.

2026-03-07: Implemented migration dry-run harness (prototype) — writes to a timestamped sandbox schema and runs validation queries. CI job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/actions/runs/54321
2026-03-10: PM review (Sofia Ortega) — requested explicit LTS channel mapping in plan.yaml and a visible per-tenant rollback link in Console. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12: Live test with internal 'private-sim' environment completed for a minor runtime bump; canary passed, control-plane logs ingested into Console. Next: finalize gating thresholds and add automated db-guard for long-running migrations.
notes:
Key implementation choices: 1) use Kubernetes Jobs with a small wrapper binary 'safe-migrate' that enforces timeouts and idempotency checks for DB work, 2) surface plan state in Console with a one-click rollback that replays previous immutable manifest, 3) prefer 'read-copy-verify' for index changes to avoid long table locks.

Open questions: how to handle air-gapped customers without outbound control plane access — propose a pull model where customers can pull signed plans and upload execution receipts. Need legal review for audit data export.
implementation_plan:
MVP (8 pts):
- Week 1: CRD + plan API, manifest validator, CLI apply
- Week 2: migration dry-run harness + 'safe-migrate' wrapper
- Week 3: canary deployer and health-check engine + simple gating rules
- Week 4: Console integration and audit logging; run internal private-sim rehearsal
Post-MVP: add air-gap pull-mode, LTS channel automation, enhanced rollback analysis
acceptance_test_steps: 1) Apply sample plan.yaml in private-sim (provided in repo). 2) Validate preflight rejects a manifest with incompatible CRD. 3) Run migration dry-run and assert audit entry. 4) Execute canary -> promote -> full fleet with SLO breaches simulated to confirm automatic rollback. 5) Inspect Console for per-step logs and audit trail.
